Smith, a 23-year-old left-hander who debuted in August, posted a 1.29 ERA in his first 19 major-league outings. In them, he pitched from an average 20.8 degree arm angle, per Baseball Savant; MLB average for left-handed pitchers this season was 37.4 degrees.

Of the 214 lefties who threw 100 pitches in the majors, just 14 averaged a release point further from the center of the mound toward first base than Smith, per Baseball Savant. He relied heavily on a slider and cutter Tuesday, and less on a four-seam fastball that was his most-used pitch during the season.

"Kind of crossfire, tough angle," Espada said. "His pitches do have some kind of difficult shape that keeps you off-balance and he did a nice job of doing that."

Smith presented some unfamiliarity. But as shortstop Jeremy Peña said: "It's the big leagues. We've got information on everybody." An Astros lineup with six right-handed hitters, still, totaled two hits against him. Smith stayed in long enough to face 11 batters, retiring nine.

He ceded to Jordan Hicks , a right-hander from Cypress Creek whose sinker averaged 100.1 mph. Hicks faced four hitters, all right-handed, and retired all of them. After Hicks got Christian Walker to ground out leading off the fifth, Venable turned to lefty Sean Newcomb for a pocket of three left-handed hitters in five spots.

The first, Lucas Spence, singled. Espada pinch-hit for the next, Taylor Trammell , with right-handed Nelson Velázquez, who hit a two-run home run. Newcomb, another low-release lefty who averaged 96.2 mph on his fastball Tuesday, retired the two other righties he faced, plus Alvarez on a ground out.

Getting through Alvarez allowed Venable to go to another right-hander, David Sandlin, who retired four of the five batters he faced, the exception a walk to Walker. Sandlin mixed five pitches while generating an average 75 mph exit velocity on four balls put into play.

"Matchups, had a lot of weapons, a lot of options," Walker said of the series of pitchers Houston faced. "Obviously, a lot of velocity. But everybody seemed to have something deceptive where the sights and the tunnels were much different. I think they did a good job of mixing guys up.

"And then obviously, the execution. Having the right matchups is only part of it. We're still a really good lineup, so to come out and execute, that's a huge part of it, too. So it's frustrating. I'm proud of our guys for fighting and clawing. Also, I guess you've got to tip your cap and give some credit when it's due."

Sandlin issued his walk in the seventh inning and a ground out moved Walker to second base with two outs. Venable said that provided the impetus to summon right-hander Grant Taylor , who finished the game for the White Sox by throwing 54 pitches and recording the final seven outs.

Of the 300 right-handers who threw at least 100 pitches in the majors this season, Taylor had the sixth-highest average arm angle, per Baseball Savant. From it, he delivered a sinker that averaged 99 mph on Tuesday, a slider that induced four whiffs on eight swings and perhaps the game's biggest pitch.

In the eighth, the Astros threatened. Peña and Alvarez, hitless in their first six at-bats, both singled. After Isaac Paredes struck out, Jose Altuve beat out a chopper to third on a wide throw, bringing the tying run to the plate with two on and two outs.

Yainer Diaz , one of the Astros' hottest hitters down the stretch, mounted a seven-pitch battle. Diaz took a 2-1 sinker at 99 mph on the corner for strike two. He spoiled a high four-seamer and took a high sinker to fill the count. Taylor landed a curveball that froze him.

One of five strikeouts for Taylor, it ended the Astros' final threat against Chicago's pitching formula, and it left them facing a must-win scenario Wednesday in this best-of-three series.

"Sometimes we have to give credit to them, and this is one of them," Diaz said, through an interpreter. "The only thing I can control was to give a good at-bat and I feel like I did that."

articles.title: Heat news: The young Miami star Giannis said is 'f***ing good'
articles.summary: MIAMI – With the Miami Heat completing their first day of training camp Tuesday, and continuing throughout the week ahead of Saturday’s preseason opener agai...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With the Miami Heat completing their first day of training camp Tuesday, and continuing throughout the week ahead of Saturday's preseason opener against the Toronto , many players are looking to fine-tune their craft before the start of the season. One of them is the Heat's young guard Pelle Larsson after signing a $60 million contract extension a week ago, as he gets the endorsement of superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo .

After a standout sophomore season for Larsson, averaging 11.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game while shooting 49.6 percent from the field, he earned himself the four-year, $60 million extension from Miami. Looking to increase his role on the Heat in his third season with open opportunity after the trade of Tyler Herro , Jaime Jaquez Jr. , and Kasparas Jakucionis , Antetokounmpo is impressed with the 25-year-old.

Speaking on Monday's media day, Antetokounmpo highlighted some players that impressed him, with Larsson being one, as the two-time Most Valuable Player (MVP) had an NSFW claim about him.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Pelle [Larsson] is f***ing good, sorry for my language, he's effin good, and I didn't know," Antetokounmpo said. "I did not know. He works hard also, has a great attitude and approach towards the game."

Heat's Erik Spoelstra on Pelle Larsson 's contract extension

Selected with the 44th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Larsson gave the Heat defensive intensity from the get-go to go along with an impressive physicality on offense, especially when driving downhill to the paint. It came together in his second season, seeing an uptick in usage, even as head coach Erik Spoelstra put him in the starting lineup 54 times last season, as he spoke about being happy for Larsson when he received the extension.

"Well, he's relentless, so he's going to make you make decisions. That's not just for the head coach; it's also the front office," Spoelstra said Monday to ClutchPoints. "He has that type of tenacity. That's why he's been such a winning player where it's been tough to keep him off the floor. Whatever that role will be, I'm sure he's going to continue to impose his will on me, on the game, and you're happy for a guy when he gets rewarded like that because we think it's well earned, and he's not going to stop."

"The way this team is built, I think fits his competitive spirit and his nature, and I think bringing out an even better version," Spoelstra continued. "He had a tremendous off-season. He was in our gym working out extremely hard, but then what he did for his national team was notable. I went and saw them play last year, and that is not easy. It's not easy to do what he did and put a team on his back and also share in their success. I think he'll be able to build off that."

Heat's Pelle Larsson on representing Sweden this past summer

As Spoelstra alluded to, Larsson took part to help the Sweden national team qualify for the 2027 FIBA World Cup, having played in four games, as he stood out in a huge way.

He was Sweden's offensive engine, averaging 26 points per game on 42.9 percent from the field, telling ClutchPoints after the first day of training camp on Tuesday that it gave him "confidence."

"Yeah, I mean we played four games trying to qualify for the World Cup next summer," Larsson said at Florida Atlantic University. "And won three out of four against very good teams, and they gave me a big role, a big load offensively, and just to score and be that guy for them, and then obviously we were successful in that, but they still got a few more games to qualify, and that just gave me confidence and that I can do more outside what I've been doing and kind of implement that from time to time in my role here."

Heat's Pelle Larsson reveals reaction to contract extension

Regarding the contract extension, which includes a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Larsson expressed how "that trust means a lot" to him from the Heat.

"Means a lot just to keep calling Miami my home and wake up here every day with a smile on my face, come to work, walk among some legends in this building, and you know, be part of that for the longer future," Larsson said to ClutchPoints Monday.

"I think I was pretty blank," Larsson continued later about his reaction. "I mean, it was not until later, I think, really when I talked to my parents, that they kind of made me realize how crazy it is. I've been playing basketball for free for most of my whole life, so to have this now is insane."

At any rate, Larsson looks to prepare for a pivotal third season in the NBA with a new-look Miami team with Antetokounmpo and others, as training camp throughout the week at FAU will be key in working toward their championship goals.

articles.title: North West 200: International road race has new date and returns to former format
articles.summary: The 2027 North West 200 international road race moves back a week to avoid a clash with the Northern Ireland Assembly and reverts back to its previous format, with qualifying commencing on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The North West 200 will move back by a week in 2027 and will revert to its previous format, with the first qualifying session taking place on Tuesday.

The change of dates is to avoid a clash with the Northern Ireland Assembly and local council elections, for which polling day is scheduled for Thursday, 6 May 2027.

As a consequence, the North West will move to the following week, with first qualifying on Tuesday, 11 May, second qualifying and the first races of the programme on Thursday, 13 May, and the main race day on Saturday, 15 May.

Roads will close at 09:00 BST on all three days, with three races again scheduled for Thursday evening and the remaining six for Saturday.

It is hoped the return to the familiar practice schedule of Tuesday and Thursday will enhance the festival atmosphere around the meeting and the area around the north coast of Northern Ireland.

Opening practice had been held on Wednesday in 2024, 2025 and 2026 to facilitate the arrival of riders and teams who were participating in the traditional May Day weekend British Superbike meeting at Oulton Park.

"We talked to a number of teams and competitors when we were across at the recent BSB round at Oulton Park, to find out what their thoughts were, and every one of them was more than pleased to go back to the Tuesday and Thursday," North West 200 Event Director Mervyn Whyte told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

"It's less issues, less problems, it's good for them, and it's good for the officials running the event because we now have a day in between.

"It will give us a longer race week festival and for us it's the right result."

Meanwhile the race organisers have secured a boost with the the news that Briggs Equipment are extending their title sponsorship agreement through to the event's centenary celebrations.

The long-term commitment mirrors the recent BBC broadcast partnership deal until the meeting's landmark anniversary in 2029.

Noussair Mazraoui is the latest Manchester United player to suffer an injury scare while on international duty.

The full-back was spotted clutching his lower back and writhing in pain on the floor after a collision during Morocco 's clash with Lesotho, which led to him being hooked in the 68th minute.

articles.title: How do teams deal with longer international window?
articles.summary: With the international window extended to four games, how do nations like Northern Ireland deal with the additional demands on players and staff?
articles.body:
In years gone by, the final whistle would have blown in Northern Ireland's Nations League game with Hungary and the players would have been heading back to their clubs.

Instead, Michael O'Neill and his squad are back on the road to Slovakia to face Ukraine in the extended international window.

For 2026, the September and October breaks have been amalgamated into one 16-day window, with four fixtures instead of two.

Northern Ireland have made a strong start to the campaign with four points from two matches, but it isn't without its challenges.

But how does it impact a nation like Northern Ireland, who do not have the squad depth or resources of some of Europe's heavy hitters?

For Northern Ireland in particular, the schedule has been gruelling.

Their Nations League campaign started with a 5,000-mile round trip to Georgia, where Shea Charles ' 99th-minute winner snatched a late victory.

For that game, O'Neill, his staff and players had stayed in the BST time zone instead of trying to adapt to the three-hour time difference.

With a short turnaround before Monday's game against Hungary - their first home match in 315 days - the squad flew back home overnight to arrive back in Belfast on Saturday morning.

While Northern Ireland kept Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai quiet - as they did with Paris St-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in Tbilisi - the players looked tired as the game progressed.

"Tiredness will be a big factor," O'Neill said.

"Logistics are a big factor as well in terms of your travel and how that works."

One other factor for smaller nations is injuries and suspensions.

Northern Ireland were already without key players such as Conor Bradley and Ali McCann before Sunderland defender Daniel Ballard injured his hamstring in Georgia, ruling him out of the rest of the window.

Unlike Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, who has the luxury of effectively selecting two different squads , O'Neill has to work with a smaller playing pool.

Of course, injuries are part of the game and can happen at any moment, but the condensed window only magnifies the issue.

"It's a massive factor in the game and if you look at some players who have been injured in the first game, like Dan, they are now out completely," O'Neill said.

"Other countries have had that as well, but you can miss four games of a six-game tournament."

Another factor to consider is an increase in yellow cards, with tired legs leading to a higher chance of picking up a second booking, which would lead to a suspension.

After two matches, seven Northern Ireland players are one card away from missing a match, and O'Neill admitted he found some of the yellows handed out to his side as "disappointing".

While this is the first iteration of the autumnal quadruple header, O'Neill says he would like to see consistency across the scheduling of matches.

Georgia, for example, have had their first two matches at home so have had limited travel and, by consequence, easier recovery from matches before they head to Hungary and Belfast for their final two games of the window.

"There are things in there that create a bit of an imbalance and I know it's difficult to get the fixtures all right," O'Neill said.

"The only thing I would like to see is we have an extra day's recovery now going into the third game.

"I would like to see the recovery periods between every game be consistent."

The consolation for Northern Ireland is that Ukraine will be making that same journey back from Tbilisi ahead of the third game, but the caveat is they have an additional day to recover and have an hour less to travel with the time difference.

O'Neill added that he understands the logic behind the scheduling, but it has "high demands on players in that time".

"It might be difficult to do that [have consistent gaps between games] but I think that would help a lot of the teams, particularly the smaller nations," he said.

"Sixteen days is a long time and there's the travel as well, obviously.

"We're coping well with it, but I think it will be a tough game for us on Friday night."

While Europe's bigger nations have their own in-house resources, countries like Northern Ireland share staff with clubs, which can bring its own challenges in an extended window.

"We don't carry full-time doctors, full-time physios and full-time sports scientists," O'Neill added.

"Other countries are the same, but all our staff work at clubs and we need agreement from the clubs.

"That's a challenge to be able to staff it properly and keep the level of professionalism.

"The big countries don't have that, they have full-time staff and an army of staff to be able to do these things."

O'Neill also has to consider how much to rotate this squad. It's a fine balance between keeping key players fresh, but also how much exposure to give his young squad.

Of the 26-man squad, 17 of the players are aged 25 or under and only three - Josh Magennis (36), Paddy McNair (31) and Dion Charles (30) - are over the age of 30.

Arsenal 's Ceadach O'Neill, Everton 's Braiden Graham and Kieran Morrison , who is on loan at Sheffield Wednesday from Liverpool, are the three teenagers in the squad.

"I don't want to put too many young players on the pitch in a game like that where they're untried and untested at that level," O'Neill said.

"We want to bring the younger players in to give them the best chance to be able to do well and to build their confidence and to build their reputation. That's the challenge for us."

articles.title: Paul Cotter scores in OT as the Canucks beat the Oilers 6-5 in the opener
articles.summary: Paul Cotter scored 1:59 into overtime to cap a two-goal game as the Vancouver Canucks got the season off to a strong start with a 6-5 win over the Edmonton O...
articles.body:
EDMONTON, Alberta (AP) — Paul Cotter scored 1:59 into overtime to cap a two-goal game as the Vancouver Canucks got the season off to a strong start with a 6-5 win over the Edmonton Oilers on Tuesday night.

Marco Rossi , Jonathan Lekkerimaki , Max Sasson and Elias Pettersson also scored for the Canucks, who are coming off a last-place finish in the NHL last season with a 25-49-8 record.

Evan Bouchard had three goals and two assists and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice for the Oilers. Tristan Jarry made 17 saves for Edmonton.

Entering the third period tied 2-2, Pettersson capped a three-goal run by the Canucks 5:15 into the frame to swiftly put the Canucks ahead 5-2.

But Podkolzin scored at 8:56, followed by Bouchard's third of the night 24 seconds later and Podkolzin's second of the night with 43 seconds left in regulation to send it to extra time.

Cotter, who joined Vancouver as a free agent after spending the last two seasons in New Jersey , became the first player in Canucks history to score a short-handed goal in his debut with the team.

Bouchard is the first defenseman in Oilers history to record a multigoal game in a season opener and just the third defenseman in NHL history to score a hat trick in an opener. He is also just the third blue-liner in the last 30 years to have at least four points in a game to open the season.

Canucks head coach Manny Malhotra became the fourth person to represent the Canucks as both a player and head coach in his career, following in the footsteps of Marc Crawford, Pat Quinn and Orland Kurtenbach.

Canucks: Host the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday.

Oilers: At the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday.

Earlier in the month, Joe Gibbs Racing announced that Jones will drive the No. 20 car full-time for the organization during the 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Series season. It has been a tough 2026 season for Jones, who was expected to be one of the championships favorites.

Jones currently sits 11th in the standings with a 114-point deficit to Sheldon Creed for the championship lead. More likely than not, Jones will not be in contention for the 2026 O'Reilly Series championship. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver has one win, six top-5 finishes, and 15 top-10 finishes.

The driver of the No. 20 car hasn't shown elite speed but it won't change his plans for the 2027 NASCAR season. Jones will be joined by Taylor Gray, Brent Crews, and William Sawalich for another campaign. To close out 2026, Jones hopes that he can end the season on a high note.

articles.title: Nuevas ayudas a los combustibles: ¿de cuánto son, de qué dependen y hasta cuándo durarán?
articles.standfirst: El Gobierno ha prorrogado unas ayudas a los combustibles que entran en vigor este 1 de octubre y que, en el caso de la gasolina, suponen una rebaja respecto a los precios actuales
articles.summary: El Gobierno ha prorrogado unas ayudas a los combustibles que entran en vigor este 1 de octubre y que, en el caso de la gasolina, suponen una rebaja respecto a los precios actuales
articles.body: Fin a la incertidumbre: el Gobierno ha decidido prorrogar a última unas rebajas fiscales a la gasolina y al diésel que caducaban este 30 de septiembre, y que tenían en vilo a miles de conductores que de pronto se temían un alza de incluso más de 20 céntimos el litro en el caso del gasóleo. Si en un principio la rebaja era de 20 céntimos/litro tanto a la gasolina como al diésel, pero luego este beneficio se fue reduciendo en el caso de la gasolina (actualmente, la primera solo está bonificada con 5 céntimos), en esta ocasión los dos combustibles vuelven a la 'casilla de salida' de las ayudas y contarán con descuentos de 20 céntimos el litro. Esto supone que el litro de diésel costará más o menos como hoy, pero también que desde el día 1 de octubre, y al menos durante un mes, la gasolina será considerablemente más barata. En concreto, repostar un depósito de 55 litros de gasolina pasará de los 104,50 euros que cuesta de media hoy 30 de septiembre a salir por unos 96,25. Es decir, más de 8 euros de descuento. Esto, sin embargo, no significa que la rebaja de 20 céntimos/litro se vaya a mantener más allá de octubre. De hecho, y como sucedía en las ayudas que hoy caducan, dependerán de la inflación. Si inflación interanual de alguno de estos carburantes supera el 15%, los incentivos para dicho combustible se mantendrán en los 20 céntimos. Pero en caso de que el 1 de noviembre esta inflación en gasolina o diésel no haya superado este 15%, la rebaja para este carburante decaerá inmediatamente al 13%. Así, llenar ese mismo depósito nos costaría de media 100,10 euros, mientras que si fuera de diésel nos saldría por 99,50 euros. De nuevo, esta rebaja tendrá la posibilidad de volver el 1 de diciembre a 20 céntimos si la inflación supera el 15%. En caso contrario, la rebaja decaerá ese mismo día hasta los 6 céntimos/litro. En estas últimas condiciones, llenar esos mismos depósitos nos costaría 103,95 euros para la gasolina y 103,40 para el diésel. Respecto a hasta cuándo durarán estas ayudas, el ejecutivo ha establecido un calendario que les pone fin el 31 de diciembre. Sin embargo, si me mantiene la cronificación del conflicto en Oriente Medio, con las conocidas dificultades de transporte por el Estrecho de Ormuz, el Gobierno podría volver a prorrogarlas en caso de que lo considerara necesario. La medida, en cualquier caso, no se puede tachar de improvisada después de que durante las últimas semanas el ejecutivo haya mantenido reuniones con los agentes sociales y el sector de las petroleras, como también ha hecho con los otros sectores energéticos afectados. Estas ayudas al sector energético (no solo a los combustibles) supondrán el desembolso de 12.000 millones de euros de las arcas públicas.

articles.title: 'Look into her eyes': Neeru Dhanda's hospital scare, 2 Asian Games golds and the 'fire' Mansher Singh saw
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda does not need to be aggressive to show her competitive side. “Look into her eyes,” says Mansher Singh, her coach of seven years.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda does not need to be aggressive to show her competitive side. “Look into her eyes,” says Mansher Singh, her coach of seven years.The 25-year-old shooter on Tuesday became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold in trap, following her World Cup triumph in Italy in July. For Mansher, who has watched Neeru develop since she was 18, the performance was another expression of a quality he has seen throughout her career.“She has a lot of fire in her belly. If in the final, she will go all guns blazing and that’s what she did,” Mansher told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.Neeru shot 28 in the final in Aichi-Nagoya, surpassing the previous Asian record of 24. She had earlier won a silver medal in the women's trap team event at the Games.The Asian Games gold came less than three months after Neeru became the first Indian woman to win an individual World Cup gold in trap, at the Shotgun World Cup in Italy. At Aichi-Nagoya, after the individual gold, she claimed her second gold in the mixed team events to add to the silver she clicnhed in the women’s team trap event.“She is not aggressive at all. If you want to see the aggression, look into her eyes,” Mansher said.“I’m just proud and happy that she’s got what she deserves because she’s very hardworking and very determined to be successful and, more importantly, to achieve. She has achieved things which have not happened in the past.”‘Winning the World Cup and Asian Games in the same year is incredible’Mansher believes the back-to-back titles have changed the conversation around his student.“So she wants to go to new heights, and this is exactly what she’s doing now. She’s won the last two big competitions. She’ll be the first Indian woman to do this, you know. So, winning the World Cup and Asian Games in the same year, almost back to back, is incredible,” he said.Neeru's rise has also been accompanied by a change in the way she handles the pressure around her.“She used to fight with me a lot. Then I would say, ‘I’m like your father.’ Then she would say, ‘Yes, I can’t fight with my father.’ Then she would come back to normal,” Mansher recalled.“But she was an emotional person. She’s much more mature now. She’s able to take her decisions and think about the consequences.”The coach was also closely involved when Neeru fell ill shortly before the Asian Games.She was admitted to PSRI Hospital in Chirag Delhi after a viral fever did not improve with medication. Even while on the hospital bed, Mansher said, Neeru remained focused on the competition ahead.“Sir, medal lana hai desh ke liye. This is all she had been saying while on the hospital bed. I was just happy and worried at the same time,” he recalled.Neeru was discharged and travelled to Japan without much time to recover.Mansher's message to her before she left was simple.“You should be happy that God has blessed you with the opportunity to go after being so sick for eight days that you were in hospital. Enjoy yourself and celebrate,” he told her.‘The Olympic medal is the first thing’With the World Cup and Asian Games titles now secured in the same year, attention will turn to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.India's last Olympic shotgun medal came through Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, who won silver in men's double trap at Athens 2004. Since then, India have not won an Olympic medal in shotgun.Mansher, who represented India at four Olympics - Los Angeles 1984, Atlanta 1996, Athens 2004 and Beijing 2008 - said the Olympic target has long been part of their conversations.“I think we don’t have to worry about that. She’s very centred. She knows that’s her goal. She’s not going to take a gold medal at the World Cup and at the Asian Games and make it so big that she loses sight of her ultimate goal,” Mansher said.“And it’s always been a conversation amongst us that, you know, the Olympic medal is the first thing. The Olympics are the first and last thing in this sport.”For Mansher, the two gold medals have provided something more useful than simply another set of titles.“But overall, there’s proof enough to say that you are definitely in that league or in that conversation to be a medalist at the Olympics,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nigeria and Ghana suffer huge AFCON 2027 qualifying shocks
articles.summary: The Gambia come back to beat ‌Ghana 4-2, while Guinea Bissau beat Nigeria 3-0 despite seven Premier League starters.
articles.body:
West ⁠African giants Ghana and Nigeria both suffered chastening defeats in Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers late Tuesday, while Algeria fought back from two goals down to avoid a shock loss to Burundi.

Tiny Cape Verde, who won legions of admirers with their gutsy exploits at this year’s World Cup, also went down in a surprise home loss to Rwanda.

But heavyweight contenders Egypt, Morocco and Senegal all won difficult away assignments, and there were home wins for Benin, Comoros, Gabon, the Ivory Coast, Mali, Mozambique, Uganda and Zambia on a busy day of 17 matches in the preliminaries for the 2027 finals to be cohosted by Kenya, Tanzania and ⁠Uganda.

Ghana, one of Africa’s 10 representatives at the World Cup where they reached the last 32, surrendered a 2-0 lead in a stunning 4-2 home defeat by The Gambia in Accra.

The Gambia, whose population is less than three million compared with Ghana’s almost 35 million, hit back through a Muhammed Badamosi penalty and goals from Omar Colley and substitute Ebrima Colley, who struck twice.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan had put the Black Stars two goals ahead after 33 minutes, but their collapse prompted angry home supporters to throw bottles onto the pitch in the closing stages.

The result ‌increased the pressure on veteran coach Carlos Queiroz after they opened their Group C campaign with a loss away to Ivory Coast last week.

Coventry City’s Yann Gboho made a dramatic debut for Ivory Coast, coming off the bench to break Somalia’s stubborn resistance in the final minute before Bazoumana Toure added a second five minutes into stoppage time to complete a 2-0 win.

Nigeria, who were semifinalists at the last Cup of Nations finals in January, had seven Premier League players in their starting lineup but were comprehensively outplayed as they went down 3-0 in Guinea Bissau, where the margin of defeat might have been even bigger.

Franculino Dju curled home the first-half opener and captain Mama Balde made it 2-0 in the 66th minute. Alvaro Djalo added a third in stoppage time.

Algeria fight back in their AFCON qualifier

Algeria found themselves 2-0 down away in Burundi after 12 ⁠minutes but fought back to share the spoils in their Group I tie in Bujumbura.

But it was a far from convincing performance ⁠under new coach Brahim Hemdani as Mohamed Belloumi and Adil Boulbina spared Algerian blushes.

Cape Verde have now lost their opening two Group K clashes after Rwanda came from one goal down to win 2-1 in Praia with teenager Elie Iradukunda netting the decisive goal. In the same group, Mali won 1-0 away in Liberia.

Egypt, who left Mohamed Salah at home over fears of potential injury on the artificial surface at Juba ⁠in South Sudan, ran out 5-0 winners with Omar Marmoush grabbing a double and Mostafa Zico, Ibrahim Adel, and teenager Hamza Abdelkarim also on target in the Group B clash.

Brahim Diaz took advantage of sloppy defending to give Morocco the lead on the stroke of ⁠halftime away against Lesotho. The match was played in Bloemfontein, South Africa, because Lesotho does not have a stadium ⁠up to international standards.

Azzedine Ounahi added a second eight minutes from time to complete the 2-0 victory that put Morocco top of Group A.

Vieira secures first victory as Senegal coach

Senegal had to defend tenaciously away against Ethiopia to give new coach Patrick Vieira his first win in charge after last week’s draw in Mozambique. Ibrahim Mbaye scored the game’s only goal after 11 minutes, having been teed up by a pass from his Aston Villa ‌teammate Nicolas Jackson.

Mozambique went top of Group J on goal difference after demolishing Sudan 4-1 in Maputo with a double from striker Chamito, who plays his club football in Portugal’s third tier.

Cameroon fought back for a 1-1 draw against Congo in Brazzaville while in the other Group G match, Comoros had a 1-0 home win in Moroni over Namibia, where ‌Benjaloud ‌Youssef scored early in the second half.

The 2012 African champions Zambia beat Togo 2-0 in Ndola in a match halted for 20 minutes by a first-half power failure. Rodolfo Aloko scored both goals for Benin in their 2-1 win over Mauritania and debutant Arnold Vula netted Uganda’s goal in a 1-0 home triumph over Libya.

articles.title: Ranking Every NHL Team's Road Jersey for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: After ranking the NHL's home jerseys recently, we had to get out there and tackle the road sweaters as well. Just as we've seen with the home jerseys, the road jerseys haven't changed from last season (apart from sponsorships in a few cases).
articles.body:
After ranking the NHL's home jerseys recently , we had to get out there and tackle the road sweaters as well. Just as we've seen with the home jerseys, the road jerseys haven't changed from last season (apart from sponsorships in a few cases).

For some of you, the road white jerseys are seen as boring because the plain white base for them makes them uninteresting. Au contraire. For a lot of teams, the white jerseys allow for more colors to breathe and other bits of creativity to shine and stripes to pop your senses.

We would love to see the white jerseys return to being worn by home teams so fans in those cities could soak in the color palettes of the visiting teams as opposed to seeing the same setup night after night at home.

However, in ranking which teams have the best (and worst) away jerseys, we learned that there are no truly bad ones, but there are some that are just so much better than the rest.

It's time to get mad (or proud), because 1 to 32, we're slotting them all in.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

Just like the Capitals home red jerseys, the white road shirts suffer from the Reebok redesign from the 2000s. There's too much piping, colors in odd places and a design of the jersey itself that takes away from all the good things (the crest logo and secondary shoulder logos) that it contains. The fonts for the numbers and letters are great, but it's just so needlessly busy otherwise. One day we'll see a change and it'll be way more fun (hopefully).

While we like Florida's home reds more than the road whites, they still rank out just above last place in our rankings.

The stripes are good, the crest logo is strong, but the busy patches and logos on the sleeves are doing too much and the numbers on the shoulders are serving football when we wanted hockey instead.

The colors are good and this style is unique to the Panthers, so they've got that going for them, but it's still just not hitting right for us.

When the Mammoth unleashed their new logo last season and with it their new home sweaters with that logo, it was a sign that great things can happen with a good-looking logo. Unfortunately, the Mammoth hung onto one part of their first season as the Utah Hockey Club with the road white sweaters and that minimalist style just doesn't do it for us.

The diagonal UTAH in team colors is fine, and putting the team logo on the shoulders was the right idea, but it feels like there were some possibilities left on the table to, ahem, jazz things up a bit.

6 Players on Trade Watch After Marchenko-Knies Deal

The Predators' road white jerseys are perfectly fine for what they need to be, but the whole of the look is screaming out for a little more color on the sleeves. Stripes, perhaps?

The shoulder yoke and the cuffs are doing the heavy lifting, but all that white space in between on the body and sleeves could use a punch up somewhere in there.

It's a total nitpick, but maybe they wanted to give fans a break from all that gold their home jerseys provide.

If we have to choose between the Lightning home and road jerseys, we're probably taking the road whites as their best ones. Yes, the look is simple for both of them, but the blue logos, stripes, numbers and lettering get a chance to pop on the white background.

Both jerseys are clean and that's always good, but there's something about Tampa Bay's road jerseys that hit a little bit harder.

Even though we're notably always down on what the Hurricanes do with their jerseys, they upgraded their road look last season by taking their Stadium Series jerseys and changing them from black to white and keeping all of the same elements.

The way the coloring on their logo is changed makes it look meaner, and that's half the battle when wearing a white sweater on the road.

It's a much better look than they used to have and for that we're all thankful.

It's kind of nutty to be this low into the rankings and have to make it clear that we don't dislike a shirt at all, but here we are with the Dallas Stars' road jerseys.

The road whites are simple and clean with the green prominently in focus on the shoulders, sleeves, numbers and names. Having the black pants and sleeve stripes to help the jersey pop more helps, but the Stars logo front and center looks great and the shoulder logos anchor things up top.

Good, easy on the eyes and flowing great on the ice is just what you want to see.

The Kraken have a solid and understated home and road set and for a new team in the league to come in looking so fresh was a huge relief.

With their logo front and center and huge on the white jersey and the layers of blue, green and red stripes up the sleeves, it gives us all the feel of the sea.

With the anchor/Space Needle logo on the shoulders, it's very Seattle without having to make use of Kurt Cobain or Jimi Hendrix.

It would've been easy enough for the Ducks to cut down on the amount of orange on their road white jerseys but we're happy they didn't because that's not a color you hide anywhere.

The Ducks went heavy on the orange with the shoulders and sleeves as well as the numbers on the road jersey. With the newly styled throwback logo on the front, you know you're dealing with the Ducks and they're proud of that.

With the black and gold mixed in with the orange and white, they might be the most distinct team to see on the road whether you like it or not.

For all the things we didn't like about the Blue Jackets' home jerseys, we really enjoy their road jerseys all the more.

Although it's tough to be your namesake on the road and having to wear white, the blue sleeves with red and white are good and the team logo crest on the front shows off nicely. We love seeing the circular logos with the cannon displayed proudly as a reminder that things would be much worse for opponents if they were in Columbus having to deal with the cannon blasts after goals.

Even though the home jerseys would be better with a simpler design, the road jerseys look great because of those same quirks.

Where the Nashville Predators' road jersey needed help, the Minnesota Wild's road jersey does the opposite.

The Wild have sleeve stripes and double stripes around the waist to go with the green shoulders. It's a solid look if not a bit basic.

If there's a knock here, it's that they only used green in the stripes on the white jersey which doesn't totally make it pop. Then again, using any amount of red would've made people wonder why the Wild celebrated Christmas year-round so... we get it.

The red numbers break up the look a little, but they don't totally alter the view.

The best part of the Senators bringing back their original look was getting to see their brilliantly good white jerseys back on the ice again.

The original logo on the front with the original shoulder logos back in place along with the red and black sleeve stripes got us in our feelings again about Peter Sidorkiewicz and Norm Maciver all over again.

It's a perfect look for Ottawa and pays homage to their history as well as allowing room for their current stars like new captain Thomas Chabot, Tim Stützle, Jake Sanderson and William Eklund to make it their own as well.

While Vegas' home gold jerseys are divisive to say the least, their road white sweaters can make everyone agree that they're quite good.

The white jerseys allow the team colors of pewter gray, gold and red to stand out proudly and the intricate design woven into the gold on the sleeves is able to grab your attention if you're into cool details.

While the gold is still all glittery and sparkling, everything else grabs attention equally thanks to the white background. Even the secondary logo on the shoulders gets a proper appearance because of it.

Much like the Avalanche's home jersey, the road jersey, despite how clean it looks, would benefit from a straightforward throwback to their original style from 1995.

The sleeve of burgundy and gray could do with a different color than gray although the shade of blue they've taken to using more wouldn't be the next choice either.

It's still a good-looking road sweater despite our grumping on some of the details, but it could be so much more.

Just like with the Islanders' iconic blue home jerseys, their road whites are just as good thanks to their simplicity. The team's fantastic crest on the front with the straight-forward blue and orange stripes and the blue collar are unmistakable as being from Long Island.

Wanting the Islanders to have more going on with either of their home or road jerseys is asking to mess with perfection and after doing that long enough ago, they won't do it again. Nor should they.

We're big fans of the Sharks' rebrand in 2022, and their road jerseys are exemplary in what it means to provide a clean look.

While the design pays homage to their original 1990s jerseys with modernized crest and shoulder logos, the teal and black stripes on the sleeves and waist help set it aside.

Their '90s jerseys had gray involved in the striping and that's gone now which gives it a starker appearance. They managed to make the Sharks look meaner and yet make the teal more omnipresent at once and that's a real accomplishment.

The Maple Leafs' iconic jersey is hard to beat and its simple style with the crest logo with blue stripes on the white jersey is something they've had in some iteration for nearly a century. When a look is that good, you try not to mess with it too much and fortunately the Leafs have left well enough alone.

Although they've tinkered around with different styles with alternate and special event jerseys, the beauty of their road whites should always remain simple and evoke the past as well as connect it to the present and future.

The beauty of the Canucks' road jerseys comes from how well the blue and green work with their entire look.

From the orca logo on the front to the original rink-and-stick logos on the shoulders to the striping on the sleeves and waist, the entirety of it is a real work of art that belongs on the Pacific coast.

What's most amazing about Vancouver's jerseys is they got 100 times better when they removed the city wordmark from above the logo on the home and road set back in 2019.

This style has been around since 2007, but was only made perfect in 2019.

As much as Detroit's home red sweaters stand out, there's something about their road white jerseys that makes the whole look work so much better.

The white jersey with the red sleeves and white stripe is a look they've had since 1956 and it's a style that's spawned countless imitators at all levels. Of course, none of those teams have the winged wheel logo on the front to grab attention and make it known who you're dealing with.

We're almost embarrassed by how much we used to dislike the Winnipeg Jets home and road set.

Maybe it had to do with debuting the look during the Reebok years and not once altering it under Adidas or Fanatics despite all the little Reebok touches that have gone by the wayside over time.

Whatever it was that made us love them initially and fall out of love with them, we've stopped being haters and the Jets' road jersey just works really well.

With the white jersey having the dark blue sleeves along with the unique sky blue and silver striping around the elbows framing the Jets logo on the front, it's just a genuinely good-looking jersey overall.

The colors are aeronautical, the logo is strong, and the shoulder logos are homey in their own way.

While the shoulder style might be a little different, the Devils' road white jerseys have been essentially the same, perfect style for 35 years. New Jersey doesn't need to oversell being the Devils.

The perfect logo on the front with black shoulders and red and black stripes on the sleeves tells you the story. That and how they've rocked this style since they stopped being a Mickey Mouse team and won multiple Stanley Cups.

The Kings' rebrand in 2024 threw it back to the 90s when Wayne Gretzky, Jari Kurri and Luc Robitaille patrolled the ice and nearly won a Stanley Cup in 1993. Doing that was a great way to get people back on board after the style they had when they won the Cup in 2012 and 2014 grew tired.

The revamped version of the 1990s logo with the silver and black color scheme screams Los Angeles, and as much as we would all love to see them bring back purple and gold a little more often, you cannot go wrong with an iconic '90s style like this.

The silver sparkles now, but don't let that distract you from how clean they look wearing these beauties.

When the Flyers changed up their home and road jerseys ever so slightly in 2023 by calling on elements of jerseys from their past, they managed to create a virtually ideal set to make everyone remember the Broad Street Bullies as well as give the current team something to build on.

The Flyers' road white jersey with burnt orange and black sleeves and the black stripe around the waist with their iconic logo at the heart of it all is one of the best looks in all of hockey.

Even fans who might not know a lot of hockey know what the Flyers look like and that it's probably about to be a really tough night.

What do you think of first when you see the Penguins rocking the white road jerseys that used to be their home jerseys in the 1990s? Is it Mario Lemieux and Jaromír Jágr? Is it The Igloo? Is it the movie Sudden Death starring Jean Claude Van Damme and Powers Boothe? Or is it Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin now that they've been wearing these since 2016?

Whatever it is, you're right to recall them fondly. They're as good as it gets with the skating penguin logo and black and gold colors on the white jersey.

While Chicago's home and road set remains one of the most identifiable and iconic jerseys in all of sports, as clean as their road white jerseys are, they're in tough competition with their home jersey for which one is best.

In this case, it's one where iron sharpens iron and has done so since 1955 when this style of sweater became their standard.

The Bruins throwing it back to the 1980s last year with their home and road set helped them find a way to modernize one of their most streamlined and perfect looks in team history.

With the black and gold stripes on the white jersey and the spoked "B" logo front and center, the Bruins got their iconic appearance back that got us all thinking about Ray Bourque and Cam Neely roaring around Boston Garden. Although the shoulder logo is a throwback to the earliest days of the franchise, the Bruins' road white jersey is unmistakably Boston all over.

The Blues changing their home and road set in full to a throwback of their inaugural jerseys was one of the best rebrands by a team in a long time.

Although St. Louis used both their blue and white jerseys in outdoor games over the past few years, bringing them together to make them their regular jerseys turned them from one of the less attractive jersey sets to one of the best.

The Blues' white road jersey with the blue and gold stripes and shoulders along with their incredible logo is straight up gorgeous. It has old-school looks but in a modern time and a design that could've stayed with them forever and been OK had they done it.

Although the Flames don't rank out quite as high for their road jerseys as they do for their home shirts, they're still one of the best in the league for a few great reasons.

The Flames' logo pops even more in its own colors on the white jersey and with the red shoulders with the red and yellow stripes on the sleeves and waist, their throwback style made new again is a true work of art.

If you want to take points off for it being a direct throwback, that's on you, but we love any style that makes us think about Al MacInnis ripping clappers from the blue line as well as the brilliance of Johnny Gaudreau.

How ever the Rangers might struggle at times, they're always going to look good win or loss and on the road is when they'll look their absolute best. Even though they're called the Blueshirts, white sweaters are what make them unforgettable.

The Rangers' road white sweaters with the red, white and blue striping on the shoulders, sleeves and waist are iconic in all ways. With the diagonal drop shadowed "Rangers" on the front and the drop shadowed numbers and letters on the back, they announce their presence everywhere they play in unmistakable style.

That this look has been virtually unchanged since the early 1950s (apart from a few years in the '70s) is what helps make it even more special.

It's hard to imagine that the Sabres ever went away from the look and style they had when they started playing in 1970, but every team tries to do something different now and again and almost always finds their way back home.

The Sabres going back to a modernized version of their original uniform set in 2021 was the best thing they could've done while things were still grim on the ice.

As good as the Sabres home royal blue jerseys are, their road white sweaters with the blue and gold shoulder yoke and sleeve stripes is what a hockey jersey is supposed to look like (especially if you grew up in the 1970s or '80s).

The way the blue and gold pops off the white jersey along with the Sabres' incredible logo makes them one of the best-looking teams to come to your town.

History goes a long way in these kinds of rankings and when history and beauty combine, it's always something special. As perfect as the Canadiens red home sweaters are, their white road jerseys are virtually just as good.

The white jersey with the red shoulder yoke, the red cuffs and the bleu, blanc et rouge stripes around the waist with the Canadiens logo in the middle of it all is what hockey history is about.

Montréal hasn't changed its road jersey since 1947 apart from the NHL mandating last names on jerseys in the 1970s and for good reason. It's perfect but among road jerseys, they're outdone by only one other team...

For everything that makes Buffalo Sabres road jerseys great, the Edmonton Oilers' road sweaters have that and then some along with more than a few Stanley Cups to make it stand up.

The Oilers' white jersey with the blue and orange shoulders as well as stripes on the sleeves and waist is iconic thanks to Wayne Gretzky, Paul Coffey, Mark Messier and all the other legends that brought the Cup to Alberta in the 80s and 1990. The orange, blue and white numbers even stand out on these beauties and it's a wonder the organization ever went away from this style at home and on the road.

Fortunately, those in charge came to their senses and brought them back again and hopefully for good because there are few greater thrills than seeing Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl roaring around the ice in these jerseys when they come to town.

articles.title: What will happen to Man City after the Premier League’s guilty verdict?
articles.summary: Man City found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. What happens next, and could they be relegated?
articles.body:
The Premier League has found Manchester City guilty of almost all of the 115 charges of breaching its financial rules in a damning verdict presented by the top flight of football in England.

The league said City broke its rules from 2009 to 2018, including by using “sham” commercial contracts “to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than 900 million pounds [$1.2bn]” of secret funding from its Abu Dhabi-based owners.

It added that the commission had found City used schemes during the affected period to appear to comply with financial rules.

“This disciplinary case and this decision are the most significant in Premier League history,” said Richard Masters, the league’s chief executive.

City, current Premier League leaders, could face punishments ranging from a fine to expulsion. The club denies wrongdoing and says it will appeal the verdict.

Here’s what we know about the charges, the verdict and possible sanctions:

What was the Premier League’s verdict on Man City’s rule breach?

Guilty on every count barring one, which was a specific failure to cooperate with the Premier League’s investigation during a portion of the proceedings. City cooperated and were found guilty.

The Premier League’s independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of financial rules across nine seasons, from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

League boss Masters said the ruling showed City “systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade”.

City, which denies any wrongdoing, said ⁠⁠it was “disappointed and surprised” by the ⁠⁠commission’s opinion.

“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its ‌‌positions, relating to this case,” it said.

City CEO Ferran Soriano called the verdict “a single false accusation” and a “Premier League conspiracy theory”.

Sponsorship deals that hid where City’s money came from.

The commission found City arranged sham commercial deals with several sponsors, who only had to pay part of the relevant sponsorship fees, as part of a “disguised funding scheme”, the league said.

The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

ADUG further funded a “sham” arrangement that enabled the club to show lower operating expenses than those it actually incurred, as well as a “sham” circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that acquired the club’s players’ image rights, which was funded by ADUG.

As a result, the club filed misstated accounts and hid its true finances from auditors and regulators. “By its conduct, the club clearly intended to circumvent” the rules, the commission said.

It is the total by which City’s schemes distorted its accounts.

The arrangements inflated revenue and reduced costs by more than 900 million pounds over the nine seasons, so the club appeared to comply with financial rules, the league said.

Of that, more than 830 million pounds ($1.1bn) was secret funding from City’s Abu Dhabi owners disguised as sponsorship.

Had City reported accurately, they would have broken spending limits “by a very substantial amount”, the commission found.

Under Rule W64 of the Premier League handbook, the commission can fine a club, deduct points or expel it from the league. A clause allowing it to “make such other order as it thinks fit” also leaves stripping titles open in theory.

The same commission will set the sanction at a separate, private hearing.

City, which called the findings “unsafe” and pledged to be “relentless” in clearing its name, must appeal by Friday. A new three-person panel will hear it.

City cannot go to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), but could challenge the process’s fairness in England’s High Court, according to British media reports.

The timing of any punishment is also contentious.

If sanctions are applied before the appeal is heard, City could be relegated only to have the verdict overturned later.

But if City are not punished until after the appeal, they could keep their points this season, costing rivals their Premier League status or a place in European competition.

What has happened to other clubs breaching Premier League rules?

Points deductions for far smaller breaches.

Everton were docked a record 10 points in 2023, later cut to six, for overspending in a single three-year period.

Nottingham Forest lost four points that season.

This year, Everton were ordered to pay Burnley more than 35 million pounds ($47m) after the latter argued it would have survived relegation in 2021-22 had Everton been punished that season.

UEFA banned City from European competitions in 2020, but CAS overturned the ban and fined City 10 million euros ($11.3m) for failing to cooperate.

City’s breaches span nine seasons and include noncooperation, making the case far wider than Everton’s.

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has said sanctions should “add a zero to what we’ve seen in terms of Forest and Everton”, suggesting 40 to 60 points, a US media outlet reported.

The outlet calculated that even 40 points would have left City 18th last season.

What could other Premier League clubs gain?

City won their first trophy in 35 years, the 2011 FA Cup, and their first Premier League title in 2012, during the period covered by the charges.

Tony Pulis, whose Stoke side lost that FA Cup final, told the BBC he did not expect trophies to change hands. “But I still feel cheated,” he said.

Could Man City lose Haaland, Cherki, Fernandez, Ndiaye, Doku?

This month, City completed the biggest spend in a single transfer window, about 460 million pounds ($610m), including Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez for $169m.

Norway striker Erling Haaland signed a nine-year contract in 2025.

It is unclear whether he or others, including Rayan Cherki, Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye, have exit clauses tied to heavy sanctions.

So far, the case has done little to stop City from attracting and keeping top players.

articles.title: “That dopamine hit needs replacing,” Kasper Schmeichel
articles.summary: Kasper Schmeichel is beginning to adjust to life after his professional playing career came to an end last season after doctors told him that he faced a seri...
articles.body:
Kasper Schmeichel is beginning to adjust to life after his professional playing career came to an end last season after doctors told him that he faced a serious of operations on his shoulder…

Kasper Schmeichel. Celtic 3 LASK 0, Champions league Playoff, Celtic Park, 19 August 2026.

The former Celtic goalkeeper played on through the pain barrier but after landing awkwardly on his injured shoulder in the Europa League play-off round against Stuttgart at Celtic Park he had to call time on his playing days on medical advice.

Now Kasper pops up on commentary duties, a role that Joe Hart also undertakes to great effect, and there are other duties Celtic's former Great Dane is now doing on a regular basis, and that's chauffeuring his three kids around!

Peter and Kasper Schmeichel speaking at the EFC General Assembly Football conference in Copenhagen. Photo EFC Football

Speaking at the EFC General Assembly in Copenhagen , Kasper Schmeichel admitted that he's practically working full-time as a taxi service at the moment!

"I have got three kids. I am a full-time Uber driver, basically," the former Celtic goalkeeper admitted. "It is a strange transition. It wasn't one I was ready for.

"Life throws these things at you, and I am adjusting. I am doing some courses, some TV work and driving the kids around. Because I didn't retire on my own terms, I still have my competitive edge." the former Celtic star admitted.

Kasper might not be able to play the game he loves any more but he's clearly far from done with football entirely. Coaching roles, even going into management are options far from being off the table.

23rd May 2026; Hampden Park, Glasgow, Scotland; Scottish Cup Final Football, Celtic versus Dunfermline; Daizen Maeda of Celtic and Kasper Schmeichel of Celtic chat on the pitch. Photograph by Vagelis Georgariou

"I would like to manage – to be a football manager or higher. The fire is still burning quite strongly," Schmeichel revealed. "I don't really enjoy getting the (coaching) badges, but you have got to get them.

"When I am on the pitch – coaching or helping youngsters coming through – I do get enjoyment out of that. My whole life I have been used to an expectation to perform, and I thrived on it.

"Now from one day to the next, that's gone. That dopamine hit needs replacing."

UEFA Champions League 2024 2025, matchday 7 Celtic Glasgow vs Young Boys Bern YB Celtic Park Kasper Schmeichel cheers his teams 1 0 victory. Photo JOERAN STEINSIEK

Whichever way Kasper goes he is sure to bring a steely determination to it and also an amazing will to win. After Joe Hart and then Kasper, the Celtic support was rather spoiled when it came to experienced, top quality keepers wearing our gloves.

5th September 2026; Paisley, Scottish Premiership, St Mirren versus Celtic; Sam Johnstone of Celtic and Viljami Sinisalo of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

For now it's a decision for Martin O'Neill whether he sticks with Viljami Sinisalo or bring back Sam Johnstone after both keepers made mistakes in the recent defeat against the latest Ibrox club.

articles.title: Ranking Jaida Parker and the Greatest WWE Main Roster Debuts by NXT Stars
articles.summary: Jaida Parker's arrival on WWE TV Monday night on Raw left the wrestling world buzzing about how bright her star might shine, not to mention its place among the other main roster debuts by NXT Superstars
articles.body:
Jaida Parker's arrival on WWE TV Monday night on Raw left the wrestling world buzzing about how bright her star might shine, not to mention its place among the other main roster debuts by NXT Superstars

From two trios who shaped the future of the industry to individual superstars who have go one to have championship-filled runs on Raw and SmackDown, who are the Superstars with the greatest first-night impressions on the WWE Universe?

Find out in this countdown, compiled based on the immediate impact of the debut, while also taking into historical context in the event of a tie.

Addressing the braggadocious claims made by the Bella Twins about championing the evolution of women's wrestling in WWE, Stephanie McMahon interrupted and introduced the next wave of competitors who would carry women's wrestling to brand new heights.

On the July 13, 2015 episode of Raw, the industry's most powerful woman introduced Becky Lynch, Charlotte Flair, and Sasha Banks to the uninitiated, kicking off the official Women's Evolution in WWE.

All three were still tied to NXT in one form or fashion, but it was clear their time on the main roster had arrived.

It was not nearly as dynamic a debut as others on this list, nor was it met with the energy or excitement that big-time arrivals by top-tier NXT women would be today, but it was absolutely essential to the long-term health and renaissance of the women's division.

All Flair, Lynch, and Banks did was go on to become three of the most decorated Superstars of any gender of their generation, with the former two making history by becoming the first to main event WrestleMania four years later.

The heart and soul of NXT during his time with the brand, Sami Zayn made an emotional and energetic debut on the main roster on the May 4, 2015 episode of Raw, live in his hometown of Montreal.

Answering John Cena's open challenge for a shot at the United States Championship, he was introduced to the crowd by the legendary Bret "Hitman" Hart and showed incredible energy as he exploded through the curtain.

Too much, as it turned out, as he suffered a dislocated shoulder before he even set foot in the ring.

Undeterred, he delivered a phenomenal performance against Cena, coming an eyelash away from dethroning him for the gold.

Despite the loss, it was a tremendous first appearance from the future two-time WWE champion and evidence of the raw emotion he would consistently bring to his performances over the next decade-plus.

There was little doubt that Paige was destined for huge things on the WWE main roster. She was treated like a star from the moment she debuted on NXT television, defeated Emma to win the vacant women's title at the brand's first live event special on the WWE Network, and was among the most popular performers on the company's developmental roster.

Somehow, that still did not prepare fans for the impact she would have right out of the gate.

On the heels of WrestleMania 30, where she successfully retained her title against the entire women's division, AJ Lee was in the midst of an ego-boosting in-ring promo when the British competitor stepped through the curtain for the first time on WWE Raw and confronted her. After being condescended to and slapped down by Lee, Paige accepted a championship match.

A few minutes later, she fought out of the Black Widow, delivered the Paige Turner, and unforgettably won the title.

The most recent entry on this list, Parker made her main roster debut in stunning fashion on the September 28 episode of Raw.

First surprising The Usos and Jacob Fatu with her appearance in a silver SUV, she claimed she was there to see Adam Pearce, presumably about an opportunity on the red brand.

Flash forward two-and-a-half hours later as she was running over Fatu in the parking lot and feigning concern before uttering the words, "no one's safe" and leaving with 946's Royce Keys in a stunning creative development.

Not only did Parker's debut take place as part of a hugely significant angle in the middle of a main event storyline, but it was met with big reactions from fans.

The audience is aware of online speculation about her off-screen relationship with Jey Uso, which earned her first appearance Monday night a nice reaction, and the ultimate betrayal later was handled so well that the audience ate it up.

It remains to be seen where things head from here but the former NXT star and former collegiate soccer player suddenly finds herself smack dab in the middle of a storyline featuring the biggest stars in the company.

It is even more impressive when considering that championship gold of any kind evaded Parker during her entire NXT run.

Before he was the prizefighter, Owens was the hottest star in NXT and one of the most buzz-about performers under the WWE umbrella. Much of that had to do with a dazzling debut that saw him beat CJ Parker (also known as Juice Robinson), then shockingly betray his best friend, Sami Zayn, later in the same show.

A great in-ring worker with an even better promo, Owens was an indy darling who had passed his first test by making an immediate impact in NXT.

There were real questions about how he would be treated on the main roster, though, thanks to long-running expectations of what a star in WWE looked like. Any concerns about his creative well-being on the main roster were eased on his first night there.

Owens debuted on the May 18, 2015, episode of Raw, confronting John Cena and answering his United States Championship Open Challenge. He laid out the industry's top star, setting up a match at Elimination Chamber, where he would defeat him and put an exclamation point on his momentous arrival.

It may have been a different incarnation of the NXT that we know and love today, but it is impossible to forget the unnerving debut of Wade Barrett, Heath Slater, Justin Gabriel, David Otunga, Michael Tarver, Skip Sheffield, Darren Young, and Daniel Bryan.

Driven for revenge after being humiliated every week during the inaugural season of NXT, the competition show designed to create the next big WWE Superstar, they attacked John Cena, CM Punk, and everyone around the ringside area in a defiant and destructive Monday Night Raw debut.

Bryan was even fired the next day for his brutal assault on ring announcer Justin Roberts, whom he choked with his own necktie and infuriated toy sponsors in the process.

Having left two of the top stars in the company lying and the ringside area utterly destroyed, they stood tall as the wrestling world buzzed about the potential creative plans for this new, invading force of nature.

Of course, history tells us that the faction was neutered in relatively short order after Cena overcame the odds and defeated them two months later in the main event of SummerSlam, but for that one moment in time, their debut shook the foundation of the WWE Universe and left fans in awe of what might have been for the new generation of developmental performers.

If fans did not know that Finn Balor was a huge deal in NXT, they found out in short order when he made his main roster debut on the July 25, 2016 episode of WWE Raw.

The former NXT champion earned a No. 1 Contender's Match right away, defeating Kevin Owens, Cesaro, and Rusev in a Fatal 4-Way Match. Later that night, the Irish-born wrestler did the seemingly unthinkable, defeating Roman Reigns to cash his ticket to SummerSlam and a chance to become the inaugural Universal Champion.

It was as emphatic a statement from WWE officials that a Superstar was to be taken seriously as a main event performer right out of the gate as we have seen in the company's modern history.

Balor would go on to defeat Seth Rollins at SummerSlam that year and win the title. Unfortunately, a devastating shoulder injury suffered during that contest would immediately put him out of action. Balor would never return to that height again, at least as of now.

Still, one is hard-pressed to find a more impressive one-night arrival than that of the Bullet Club's founding member.

Roman Reigns, Seth Rollins, and Dean Ambrose exploded onto the scene in WWE at the 2012 Survivor Series, interfering in the night's main event and assisting CM Punk in retaining his WWE Championship.

It was a momentous and buzzworthy debut for the trio, who drove Ryback through the announce table, which allowed Punk to cover a fallen John Cena and win the high-stakes Triple Threat Match.

The WWE faithful were intrigued by the trio's arrival and eager to find out the reasoning for their actions. There was genuine intrigue about a product that lacked it at the time.

Little did fans know that those three Superstars jumping the guardrail that night and beating down Ryback would change the course of professional wrestling history as Reigns, Ambrose, and Rollins would define the company's next era.

articles.title: LeBron James’ Risky Post-Practice Decision Has Fans Saying ‘Be Careful We Already Lost One Legend’
articles.summary: LeBron James is building his post-Lakers life around New York, about 95 miles from the Philadelphia 76ers‘ practice facility in Camden, New Jersey. James, 41...
articles.body:
LeBron James is building his post- Lakers life around New York, about 95 miles from the Philadelphia 76ers ' practice facility in Camden, New Jersey. James, 41, told ESPN's Dave McMenamin on Monday that he has "multiple residences" and will live in both cities this season.

By car, the trip takes 90 minutes to two hours each way. Every practice or home game outside the Philly area could eat three to four hours round trip, so James found a shortcut on Tuesday.

Bleacher Report's McMenamin reported that a helicopter waiting for James could be heard outside the facility while Anfernee Simons spoke to reporters after the Sixers' first training camp practice Tuesday.

He wrote on X, "While Anfernee Simons was answering questions to the media members after Sixers practice Tuesday a loud droning noise could be heard coming from outside the facility: a helicopter for LeBron James to take to head to New York."

A helicopter easily covers the same distance James needs to travel in just 40 to 45 minutes. However, whenever NBA fans hear about players using helicopters, they are instantly reminded of the tragedy that took the life of Lakers legend Kobe Bryant.

Fans unload on LeBron James' post-practice chopper ride to New York

Fans on X criticized LeBron James' decision to commute by helicopter, expressing anxiety due to Kobe Bryant 's tragic death in a 2020 helicopter crash.

One fan wrote , "Be careful we already lost one legend…"

Another posted , "Still taking a helicopter huh? Can't see anything going wrong thats for sure."

A third asked , "Helicopter rides after what happen to Kobe?"

The fourth one penned , "Careful, helicopters and basketball players don't mix."

A random X user noted , "Seems crazy high risk to save 35 minutes vs other means of transportation."

The backlash traces back to January 26, 2020. That was the day Kobe Bryant, his 13-year-old daughter Gianna, and seven others died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California. Following the tragedy, aviation attorney and former Marine pilot Justin Green explained that poor visibility can easily cause pilots to lose their bearings.

The flight path between Philadelphia and New York often deals with harsh winter weather, heavy fog, and sudden icing. Still, sports outlets note there is no proof that LeBron's specific flight plan is actually unsafe.

articles.title: Yankees’ next generation is already crushing it: Red Sox (and Rays) beware | Klapisch
articles.summary: The Yankees didn't need the help of their veteran stars to find themselves at the doorstep of the Division Series.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — If I'm the Red Sox , I'd be awfully worried about how easily the Yankees rolled to a 9-0 wipeout in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. The gap between the two teams is so vast it would be naïve to think the Yankees aren't already looking ahead to the Division Series against the Rays.

The Red Sox, after all, had no answers for the Yankees on either side of the ball. Cam Schlittler destroyed Boston 's lineup – 6 1/3 innings, two hits, one walk, 10 strikeouts – while Ben Rice made everyone forget about Aaron Judge for 24 hours. Rice went 4-for-5 with two home runs (one was a grand slam) with six RBIs.

Manager Aaron Boone wasn't exaggerating when he called it a "special night" in the Bronx. The Yankee Stadium crowd was alive, and Rice's solo blast in the fifth inning was all it took to ignite it. The Yankees took that momentum and ran with it for the rest of the evening. It wasn't just the Red Sox who were being schooled – the message was sent all the way to Florida.

That should be the Rays' primary concern. When the Yankees set foot in Tropicana Field on Saturday night, they'll be led by the emerging next generation. From Rice to Schlittler, from George Lombard Jr. to Spencer Jones, and even the re-emergent Anthony Volpe . It's hard to disagree with Boone when he says, "We're a confident group … if we play our game, we can beat anyone."

There was no overt disrespect to the Red Sox, who were the American League's third-best team this season. But the humiliation on Tuesday went beyond the box score. Getting squashed by Schlittler and Rice — two native New Englanders whom the Sox chose not to draft out of college — was like rubbing it in Boston's face.

What a narrative for the Yankees — and the source of unending embarrassment for the Red Sox.

"This definitely adds a cool little layer to it, and for Cam, too," Rice said. "It's always fun playing against them. Having a solid game against them is pretty cool."

As fierce a hitter as Rice is, he's one of the gentlest souls in the Yankees' clubhouse. He's not mad at the Sox for letting him slip away. To the contrary, Rice grew up a Yankees fan who "idolized" Derek Jeter . He still gets a laugh remembering he wore a Yankees jacket for a first-grade class picture.

Schlittler, on the other hand, runs on darker fuel. He'll never forgive the Sox for dismissing him as a college pitcher who didn't throw hard enough. He lives for revenge these days. Schlittler gets pleasure from taking and returning fire with Sox fans on social media.

"I wouldn't say I'm always on my phone looking for that stuff," Schlittler said. "At the same time, I don't really live under a rock, as well. So finding ways to use that to my advantage, and I think I'm good at keeping receipts."

Schlittler has made the Sox pay — over and over. In his two-year career, Schlittler has posted a 0.47 ERA against Boston, striking out 49 in 38 2/3 innings. He's never allowed the Red Sox more than one earned run in any game he's pitched.

On Tuesday, Schlittler generated a career-high 24 swings and misses. The metric needs no other translation. Schlittler toyed with the Sox. It wasn't just from elite velocity, either.

Even though his fastball averaged 98.6 mph on the radar gun, Schlittler's best weapon was the 32 curveballs that paralyzed Boston's hitters.

The pitch broke sharply with late, downward movement. The book on Schlittler advises "cheating" on his four-seamer – in other words, swing early. That's the only way to catch up to one of the AL's premier fastballs. But doing so allowed Schlittler to short-circuit the Red Sox's timing.

Swing and miss. Swing and miss. Swing and miss.

No wonder Schlittler was celebrated as a hero when he finally walked off the mound in the seventh inning. It felt like the start of a beautiful relationship. He and Rice are learning that there are two critical components to becoming a Bronx legend: beat the Red Sox and do it in October.

The first box is almost checked. The second is a work in progress, but there's every reason to believe the 25-year-old Schlittler and the 27-year-old Rice will be leading the Yankees well into the next decade.

The Yankees' old guard will be gone by then. Judge (34), Gerrit Cole (36) and Giancarlo Stanton (37 in a few weeks) will all be Hall of Fame candidates, though they have so far failed to deliver a championship. That white whale might have to be chased by the next generation.

In the meantime, though, the Yankees are working on two other boxes.

Finish off the Sox and prepare for war with the Rays. It starts Saturday night.
