articles.title: Towns Wants To Stay, But Knicks Must Fix The Apron First
articles.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns says he wants to re-sign, but the second apron rules could block a $276 million deal. Here is why the Knicks face a tough choice.
articles.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns has made his stance clear at the Tarrytown media day on Monday. He wants to stay in New York and get a new deal done before the season starts. However, the rules of the league might force the Knicks to say no to his request. Towns is eligible for a massive four-year contract worth over $276 million, but the team is already deep in the salary cap trouble.

Towns is not hiding his feelings about the franchise. He told reporters on Monday that he has been a Knicks fan since he was just a kid. He said he wants to "get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible." The star center knows that uncertainty can hurt the team's chemistry during a title defense run. He even noted that the group has done a "fantastic job of understanding that we can only control what we can control."

But comfort is hard to find when the contract situation remains open. Towns admitted that the current setup creates stress for everyone involved. He said, "In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had." The Knicks won their first title in 53 years last season, and Towns was a huge part of that success. He averaged 15.9 points and 10.6 rebounds while the team ended a long drought. Keeping him makes sense on the court, but the business side is messy.

The real problem for the Knicks is not Towns' desire to stay. It is the strict financial limits placed on teams that spend too much money. $57 million is owed to Towns this season, while he holds a $61.1 million player option for the upcoming year. Adding his new extension would push the team deep into the punitive second apron. Mitchell Robinson , the Knicks' backup center, has already been lost to this rule after signing with the Boston Celtics this summer.

Towns knows the rules are tough, but he also knows they are confusing for players. He told ESPN that he cannot explain the complex financial details. "You ask me to give three facts or two facts about the second apron, I can't do it," Towns said. He added that he has no interest in learning the fine print because it is just "what it is." The team president Leon Rose trusts him on the court, and Towns trusts him back. But the league rules do not care about trust.

Josh Hart , another starter with a looming contract, warned that rumors can wear people down. He said that uncertainty leads to questions that affect how players handle business every day. The Knicks hope to break the trend of eight different champions in eight years, but the salary cap makes that goal harder.

The Knicks must decide if they will pay Towns the full amount or risk losing him later. Towns has a player option for next season, which gives him some control. If he declines the option, he becomes a free agent. If he takes it, he gets paid $61.1 million while the team waits to see if an extension is possible. The team reshuffled the roster by adding center Andre Drummond to bolster the bench.

Towns said he wants to talk about everything and not leave any elephants in the room. He believes the front office will figure out the money issues. But the clock is ticking fast. The season starts soon, and the distraction of a contract dispute could hurt the team's chances to defend their title. The Knicks have a champion core, but the second apron rules might force them to break it up before they even try.

articles.title: Where Jalen Hurts ranks among NFC East QBs after Week 3
articles.summary: A stunning Commanders victory shakes up this week's rankings as the Eagles and Cowboys search for answers after tough losses.
articles.body:
The NFC East delivered plenty of drama in Week 3. The Philadelphia Eagles didn't produce much on offense. Marcus Mariota delivered one of the weekend's biggest surprises, leading the Washington Commanders to an upset over the Seattle Seahawks .

Then, there's Jameis Winston . The New York Giants have acquired J.J. McCarthy , but before that, they improved to 2-1 with a victory over the Tennessee Titans , led by Winston's on-field leadership.

Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys left Brazil wondering what might have been after a heartbreaking loss to the Baltimore Ravens . Two NFC East quarterbacks walked away with victories. Two didn't. As the division heads into Week 4, here's how the quarterbacks stack up after another eventful weekend.

1. Marcus Mariota, Washington Commanders

You probably didn't expect to see Marcus Mariota this high when the season began. No, he isn't better than Jalen Hurts or Dak Prescott, but the NFL is a week-to-week league. If we knew nothing about these quarterbacks before Week 3, we'd have to say Mariota was the best of the four.

Now, that may change in Week 4. It probably will, but that's where we are today.

Mariota authored one of the biggest wins of Week 3, helping Washington knock off ​the defending-champion Seahawks , a team many believed would handle the Commanders at home. This wasn't a case of Washington surviving mistakes or benefiting from a fluky bounce. Mariota made timely plays and delivered when his team needed him most.

He completed 19 of 31 passes for 183 yards and three touchdowns while avoiding turnovers. He also added 11 rushing yards, including a key late scramble that helped position Washington to close out a 33-31 victory. The raw passing yardage won't wow anyone, but Mariota did the most important job a quarterback can do: he elevated his team against quality competition.

His 61.2 QBR and 110.0 passer rating reflect an efficient and winning performance that deserves recognition.​ So, think about this for a second. Washington has the Indianapolis Colts at home in Week 4. What happens if the Commanders win two straight?

Dak Prescott falls a spot this week, but not because he played poorly. The veteran quarterback threw for 276 yards and a touchdown while posting a respectable 63.6 QBR and 91.2 passer rating. For much of the afternoon, he did enough to position Dallas for a statement victory over Baltimore.

Unfortunately for Prescott, the game's lasting image came on the Cowboys' final offensive possession. Facing third-and-goal from the two-yard line with seconds remaining, Prescott threw the ball out of bounds while George Pickens appeared open near the front pylon.

Dallas eventually tied the game with a field goal, but Baltimore answered with a walk-off kick moments later. Prescott remains one of the division's most talented quarterbacks, but the late-game sequence, combined with Dallas' 1-2 record, nudges him behind Mariota this week.

Jalen Hurts lands third after a frustrating night in Chicago . The Eagles quarterback completed 16 of 25 passes for 153 yards, no passing touchdowns, one interception, and a 64.2 passer rating while adding 25 rushing yards and Philadelphia's lone touchdown on the ground.

There were a few bright spots. Hurts connected with DeVonta Smith on another beautiful deep ball and looked sharp during the Eagles' final drive of the first half. Unfortunately, those moments were far too brief. Philadelphia's offense disappeared during the second half, and Hurts' fourth-quarter interception to T.J. Edwards ended any realistic hopes of a comeback.

The loss wasn't entirely on Hurts. The defense struggled, the running game vanished after halftime, and the coaching staff will face questions about the game plan. Still, franchise quarterbacks are judged by results, and the Eagles managed only seven points in a game that quickly slipped away. That drops Hurts to third in this week's rankings.

A win is a win, and Winston deserves credit for helping the Giants improve to 2-1. That said, his performance against Tennessee won't be remembered as one of the season's masterpieces. Winston completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards, failed to throw a touchdown pass, and finished with a 27.9 QBR and 77.5 passer rating.

The Giants found a way to win, which ultimately matters most. Still, when comparing the four quarterbacks in the division, Winston's Week 3 body of work was the least impressive statistically.

New York won't spend much time apologizing for a victory, but Winston remains fourth in this week's rankings despite the result.

articles.title: Pirates focused on putting heavy loss behind them
articles.summary: Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are focused on putting their 73-40 loss at Coventry behind them.
articles.body:
Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are focused on putting their 73-40 loss at Coventry behind them.

Coventry scored 11 tries as Pirates suffered one of their heaviest defeats in a Champ fixture.

The loss came a week after an impressive opening weekend win over Doncaster at the Mennaye Field.

"The boys are motivated, you don't become a bad team overnight," Cattle told BBC Radio Cornwall.

"When you win you think you're better than you are and when you lose you think you're worse than you are.

"So it's just a bit of a reality check to focus on what we're doing, what we've been doing in training and let's get some transfer."

Pirates' campaign does not get any easier as they host last season's table-toppers Ealing on Saturday.

Cattle feels that the heavy scoreline did not tell the whole story of his side, who conceded almost half of their points in a 15-minuyte spell around two yellow cards.

They had injury problems in the warm-up and still scored six tries at a side that finished third last season and made the play-off semi-finals.

"You can see the 70 points, obviously something drastically has gone wrong," he added.

"I think the pivotal point was the second yellow card, going down to 13 men.

"I'm not one to go down the referee route, but I can't see why that was a yellow card in my eyes and I think that was a real pivotal point, especially when we had a lot of late change in the backline.

"We conceded 30 points in that period. Could we have managed it better? There's definitely some learning there, but when we had 15 men on the pitch, not only were we competitive, we looked in patches very good."

It means there will be a motivated Cornish Pirates side that host an Ealing team that have not lost a regular-season game since April 2025.

"There's a lot of boys who want to put things right," added Cattle.

"Coaches, players, we all want to put our best foot forward and try and emulate the performance we put against Doncaster.

"This is a chance to get more cohesive, build different combinations.

"Is it going to be polished? I doubt it, but is it going to be full of heart, emotion, want to put things right? That gives you a lot on a day and I think you'll see a good response from our lads."
